newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal govt concessions do not hurt EMU chances.
newsitem.headline: Portugal govt concessions do not hurt EMU chances.

text.p: Measures proposed by the small Popular Party (PP) in return for allowing the 1997 budget to pass will not affect Portugal's chances of joining the European single currency, Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said.
"(These proposals represent) less than 0.1 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and our target to cut the budget deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP next year is not at risk," he told Reuters.
The government accepted specific recommendations by the PP including smaller minimum tax payments by shop owners and the abolition of a stamp duty.
The budget is expected to be passed in a final parliamentary vote on December 12 after the PP, who have 15 seats in the 230-seat chamber, agreed to abstain.
The government aims to cut the budget deficit to 2.9 percent of GDP next year from about four percent this year.
